issues.current_content:
# Basics

This chapter covers the basic usage of ripgrep, including pattern matching, literal strings, and regular expressions.

*This content will be populated by the documentation drift detection workflow.*
issues.should_add: Complete chapter content covering pattern matching, literal strings, regular expressions, and output formats with working examples
issues.fix_suggestion: Populate the entire chapter with foundational ripgrep usage documentation

issues.description: No explanation of basic pattern matching syntax and usage
issues.should_add: Basic pattern matching examples: simple searches, how ripgrep interprets patterns by default, pattern specification with -e/--regexp flag
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section explaining basic pattern syntax with examples like 'rg TODO', 'rg -e pattern1 -e pattern2', and 'rg -f patterns.txt'

issues.description: No documentation of fixed string search mode for literal matching
issues.should_add: Fixed string search documentation explaining when and how to use -F/--fixed-strings flag
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section on literal string matching: 'rg -F "function()"' vs 'rg "function\(\)"', explain when to use -F to avoid regex interpretation, show performance benefits

issues.description: No introduction to regex syntax supported by ripgrep
issues.should_add: Regular expression basics for ripgrep: Rust regex syntax overview, common patterns, basic metacharacters, character classes, quantifiers
issues.fix_suggestion: Add comprehensive regex introduction: basic metacharacters (., *, +, ?, ^, $), character classes ([a-z], \d, \w, \s), quantifiers, groups, escaping special characters. Include examples: 'rg "[0-9]+"', 'rg "\bword\b"', 'rg "error.*failed"'
issues.source_reference: features.json:regex_support (Rust regex syntax, Unicode support, case folding)

issues.description: No documentation of output format options and how results are displayed
issues.should_add: Output format basics: default output format, line numbers, file names, colors, basic formatting options
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section on output formatting: default grep-like output, -n/--line-number for line numbers, --column for column numbers, color output (--color), heading vs non-heading modes. Show examples of what output looks like with different options
issues.source_reference: features.json:output_formatting (Standard grep-like output, line numbers, colors, heading mode)

issues.description: No documentation of case sensitivity control options
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section on case sensitivity: default behavior (case-sensitive), -i for case-insensitive search, -S/--smart-case (case-insensitive if pattern is all lowercase), examples showing difference between 'rg TODO', 'rg -i todo', 'rg -S Todo'

issues.description: No documentation of word boundary matching options
issues.should_add: Word boundary matching: -w/--word-regexp for whole word matches, -x/--line-regexp for whole line matches
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section on boundary matching: -w to match whole words only ('rg -w test' won't match 'testing'), -x to match entire lines only. Show examples demonstrating the difference

issues.description: No working examples demonstrating basic ripgrep usage
issues.should_add: Practical examples showing common use cases for beginners
issues.fix_suggestion: Add examples section with: simple search 'rg pattern', search in specific files 'rg pattern file.txt', case-insensitive search 'rg -i pattern', literal string search 'rg -F "exact string"', count matches 'rg -c pattern', list matching files 'rg -l pattern'

issues.description: No documentation of basic count and list modes
issues.should_add: Count modes (-c/--count, --count-matches) and file listing modes (-l/--files-with-matches, --files-without-match)
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section showing: -c to count matching lines per file, --count-matches to count individual matches, -l to list files with matches, --files-without-match to list files without matches

issues.description: No documentation of inverted matching with -v flag
issues.should_add: Inverted matching: -v/--invert-match to show lines that don't match
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section on inverted matching: -v flag to show non-matching lines, useful for filtering out lines ('rg -v "debug"' to see all lines without 'debug')
